abstract_sentences.text: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) are promising alternatives to autoregressive large language models (AR-LLMs), as they potentially allow higher inference throughput.
Reinforcement learning (RL) is crucial to enabling dLLMs to achieve performance comparable to that of AR-LLMs on important tasks, such as reasoning.
However, RL algorithms well-suited to dLLMs’ unique characteristics have yet to be developed.

This paper proposes Distribution Matching Policy Optimization (DMPO), a principled and theoretically grounded RL fine-tuning method specifically designed to enhance the reasoning capabilities of dLLMs by matching the dLLM policy distribution to the optimal, reward-tilted one through cross-entropy optimization.
We identify a key implementation challenge with small training batch sizes and propose several effective solutions based on a novel weight baseline subtraction technique.

DMPO exhibits superior performance on multiple reasoning benchmarks without supervised fine-tuning, achieving up to a 39.63 percentage-point improvement in accuracy over prior non-DMPO RL baselines and 67.97 percentage points over the base model, underscoring the effectiveness of the distribution-matching framework.
Our code is available at https://github.com/yuchen-zhu-zyc/DMPO.

experimental_design.name: Pre-registered research questions
experimental_design.description: No preregistered hypothesis list is stated; Section 4 is organized by model/baseline, setup, and result prose.

experimental_design.name: Training backbones
experimental_design.description: DMPO is applied to LLaDA-8B-Instruct and Dream-Instruct (7B) without an initial SFT phase for the primary pipeline.

experimental_design.name: Baselines
experimental_design.description: The paper names Dream-Instruct, LLaDA-Instruct, LLaDA-1.5, d1, cGRPO, wd1, and GDPO as comparisons.

experimental_design.name: Tasks and metric
experimental_design.description: GSM8K, MATH500, Countdown, and Sudoku are used; primary tables show accuracy.

experimental_design.name: Train/test and explicit evaluation denominators
experimental_design.description: GSM8K/MATH500 use train/test splits; MATH500 contains 500 problems; Countdown and Sudoku evaluate 256 generated instances each.

experimental_design.name: Reward construction
experimental_design.description: GSM8K and MATH500 use format/correctness rewards; Countdown checks the equation; Sudoku reward is the fraction of original blanks correctly filled.

experimental_design.name: Fair-comparison controls
experimental_design.description: DMPO-LLaDA/Dream are trained on the same task datasets as d1 with fixed rollout length 256 and evaluated zero-shot.

experimental_design.name: Evaluation decoding
experimental_design.description: LLaDA-series uses lengths 128/256/512 and Dream uses 256/512; Appendix C.2 gives samplers, temperatures, and remasking.

experimental_design.name: Training hyperparameters and hardware
experimental_design.description: TRL, LoRA rank 128/scaling 64, 8 H100 or H200 GPUs, AdamW settings, 16 rollouts per prompt, and 4,000 updates are stated.

experimental_design.name: d1 reproduction
experimental_design.description: The d1 reproduction first performs SFT on s1k and trains up to 13,000 iterations under the cited guidelines.

experimental_design.name: Random seeds and repeated runs
experimental_design.description: No seed values, run count, or seed-level outcomes are stated in the reported experimental setup.

experimental_design.name: Uncertainty/statistical inference
experimental_design.description: Tables give point estimates; the paper does not state a test, interval, multiple-comparison procedure, or effect-size protocol.

experimental_design.name: Human evaluation
experimental_design.description: No human-evaluation method is described in the experiment section or Appendix C.

experimental_design.name: Explicit data-leakage control and failure criterion
experimental_design.description: The PDF specifies train/test splits and synthetic evaluation generation but does not state a separate leakage-control procedure or a predeclared failure criterion.

claim_closure.claim: Distribution matching should replace reward maximization as the organizing target.
claim_closure.method_response: Eqs. (5)–(11) define p* and WDCE; Figure 2 gives the mode-seeking/mass-covering intuition.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 9 gives one sequential-entropy comparison, not a direct response-distribution estimate.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 5 restates matching a reward-tilted distribution.

claim_closure.claim: DMPO is a principled dLLM RL fine-tuning strategy.
claim_closure.method_response: MDM/ELBO, importance sampling, WDCE, Algorithm 1, and Appendix B specify the procedure and derivation.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Tables 1–2 cover LLaDA and Dream across four tasks.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 5 repeats the framework and its forward/off-policy properties.

claim_closure.claim: Weight-baseline subtraction and WDDO address the small-batch challenge.
claim_closure.method_response: Eqs. (12)–(16) and Figure 3 specify the correction and its rationale.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 4 tests alternatives on Sudoku; Figure 7 adds a limited N sensitivity study.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 5 refers generally to the framework, not a separate small-batch boundary.

claim_closure.claim: DMPO improves reasoning accuracy and efficiency over listed baselines.
claim_closure.method_response: Off-policy WDCE and forward computation are the stated efficiency mechanism.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Tables 1–2 and Figure 5 supply the reported accuracy and PF-day comparisons.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 5 restates effectiveness but adds the two-backbone/four-benchmark scope boundary.

claim_closure.claim: Cross-entropy matching maintains higher diversity and avoids mode collapse.
claim_closure.method_response: Forward KL is described as mass-covering; Appendix B derives a target path measure.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 9 measures sequential entropy in one configuration.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion does not add a direct diversity metric or boundary.

final_judgment.single_storyline: dLLM 的 masked/random-order 特性使 GRPO-style likelihood approximation 昂贵且可能偏向 reward modes；DMPO 以 reward-tilted p*、WDCE 和 baseline correction 连起目标、可训练损失、小-batch 修正与 benchmark evidence。【pp. 1–9, §§1–5】
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: 主文保留问题、p*、WDCE、baseline 直觉、Figures 1–5、Tables 1–2、compute comparison 和明确范围限制。【pp. 2–9】
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix 承担 Algorithm 1、related-work taxonomy、CTMC/SOC proof-style derivation、rewards/hyperparameters、additional curves/ablations 与两个样例。【pp. 16–26】
final_judgment.best_pattern: 先以 Figure 1 交付跨任务结果，再用 Figure 2/3 解释 target 与 small-batch mechanism，最后以表格和效率曲线回收；顺序为现象、目标、损失、修正、结果。【pp. 2–9】
final_judgment.largest_gap: 明示范围仅 two backbones/four elementary tasks；tables 没有 seeds/repetitions/inference details，Figures 4–8 的 bands 未定义，entropy 只在一个 configuration 中出现。【pp. 8–9, 23–24】
final_judgment.transfer_rule: 对于有明确 distributional target 的算法论文，连续呈现 target、computable surrogate、known failure condition、component control 和 task evidence，使 Eq. (5)→Eq. (11)→Figure 3/4→Tables 1–2 可顺序复核。
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: 此规则适用于有形式化 target、可实现 loss 和可观察组件对照的工作；开放式偏好或缺少可拆组件的研究需要不同的证据链。这是基于本文结构的解释，非作者主张。
